paragraphs: Since 2023 Cumbria has had two councils, Cumberland and Westmorland and Furness, and they share one fostering service, Cumbria Fostering. Children in care here are looked after by that service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. In May 2026 Cumberland Council said there were around 730 children in care in Cumbria and around 275 carers, and that the greatest need was for brothers and sisters, older children and children with more complex needs.

The councils' sufficiency strategy for 2024 to 2027 recorded 219 mainstream foster families, with eight households joining over a year and 18 leaving, mostly through retirement. It names the homes most needed: carers for disabled children, teenagers, larger sibling groups and young people who arrived in the UK alone, and carers who can look after a parent with their baby. In January 2026 Cumbria Fostering launched a campaign to tackle five common myths, about age, working, money, being LGBTQ+ and disability, that stop people enquiring.

Enquiries are handled with help from Foster With Us, a recruitment hub set up in July 2024 with Lancashire, Blackpool and Blackburn with Darwen councils, though each council still carries out its own assessments. In October 2024 Cumbria Fostering began the Mockingbird programme, in which an experienced hub carer supports a small group of six to ten fostering families; the first groups started in Workington and Barrow. The councils describe round-the-clock support, training on trauma and life story work, and support groups for carers.
Cumbria is large and rural, so ask any service you speak to, council or agency, how far children usually travel to school and family time, and what training and support is available near you.
